cases.name: Santa Fe Independent School District v. Doe

components.decision: The Court invalidated the school’s student-led, student-selected prayer policy before football games.
components.scope: The school policy and public-address setting mattered; this was not a ban on students praying privately.
components.survey_fit: The poll asks about graduation, not football games, and omits the election and public-address arrangements. It is contextual, not a measure of approval of this ruling.

observations.wording: Permitting student prayer within the official graduation program.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased question. The source marks no opinion with an asterisk (less than 0.5%). The numeric zero is a lower bound for validation, not an observed zero. The 2000 article verifies the 1999 sample; the PDF’s 2014 sample does not apply.
observations.denominator: National sample of 1,016 adults; original response shares retained.
observations.orientation: Policy context only; not approval of the specific holding.

cases.name: Good News Club v. Milford Central School

components.issue: Religious viewpoint in an after-school forum
components.decision: Excluding the club because of its religious viewpoint violated the Free Speech Clause.
components.scope: Access for a private club in a limited public forum, not school-led religious instruction.
components.locator: Syllabus, holdings 1–2; Thomas opinion, Parts II–IV.
components.survey_fit: The question describes student religious groups. The case involved an adult-led Christian club for children aged 6–12, so the match is contextual.

observations.wording: Allowing student religious groups to use school facilities after hours.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased question. Article reports the full national sample of 1,016 adults. This later pre-ruling observation supersedes the 1999 after-hours question for Good News Club.
observations.denominator: National sample of 1,016 adults; original response shares retained.
observations.orientation: Policy context only; not approval of the specific holding.

limitations: Explicit source-based legal coding is an input, not an automated legal classifier.
